authors: Sho Kobayashi; Takujiro Homma; Junichi Fujii

abstract: This study investigated the role of nitric oxide (NO) in protecting macrophages from superoxide toxicity. NO produced by NOS2 was found to counteract superoxide's cytotoxic effects, particularly under inflammatory conditions.

authors: Rachel Young; Stephen J. Bush; Lucas Lefevre; Mary E. B. McCulloch; Zofia M. Lisowski; Charity Muriu...
abstract: This study analyzed gene expression related to nitric oxide production in macrophages from various species. Macrophage responses to LPS stimulation, including NOS2 induction, are not conserved across species and may be influenced by retrotransposon insertions.

authors: Chun-Yu Lin; Shih-Han Kao; Ling-Chien Hung; Hsin-Ju Chien; Wen-Hung Wang; Yu-Wei Chang; Yen-Hsu Chen

abstract: Tellimagrandin II was studied for its anti-inflammatory effects on macrophages stimulated by lipopolysaccharide. TGII significantly inhibited nitric oxide and prostaglandin E2 production by reducing key inflammatory signaling pathways.

title: Dataset on the differentiation of THP-1 monocytes to LPS inducible adherent macrophages and their capacity for NO/iNOS signaling
authors: Adem Ozleyen; Yakup Berkay Yilmaz; Tugba Boyunegmez Tumer
abstract: This study details optimized conditions for differentiating THP-1 monocytes into adherent macrophages and inducing inflammatory responses. The differentiated cells exhibit significant NO/iNOS signaling and altered expression of pro-inflammatory genes upon LPS stimulation.

title: A Defective TLR4 Signaling for IFN-β Expression Is Responsible for the Innately Lower Ability of BALB/c Macrophages to Produce NO in Response to LPS as Compared to C57BL/6
authors: Luciana S. Oliveira; Nina M. G. P. de Queiroz; Laura V. S. Veloso; Thaís G. Moreira; Fernanda S. Oli...
id: Matched: Differential production of NO in C57BL/6 and BALB/c macrophages correl
abstract: BALB/c macrophages produce less NO than C57BL/6 macrophages upon LPS stimulation due to a defective TLR4-induced IFN-β signaling pathway. This defect impairs STAT-1 activation, leading to lower iNOS mRNA and protein levels.

title: Neutrophilic granule protein promotes lipopolysaccharide-induced iNOS/NO expression via JAK2/STAT1 signaling pathway and augments bacteria clearance of macrophages
authors: Lixing Tian; Shuangqin Yin; Jing Wang; Hongyan Xiao; Tianyin Kuang; Li Luo; Shengxiang Ao; Jing Zhou...

abstract: Neutrophilic granule protein (NGP) was studied for its role in macrophage response to lipopolysaccharide (LPS). NGP enhances LPS-induced nitric oxide production via the JAK2/STAT1 pathway, promoting bacterial clearance.

title: Pheophytin a Inhibits Inflammation via Suppression of LPS-Induced Nitric Oxide Synthase-2, Prostaglandin E2, and Interleukin-1β of Macrophages
authors: Chun-Yu Lin; Chien-Hsing Lee; Yu-Wei Chang; Hui-Min Wang; Chung-Yi Chen; Yen-Hsu Chen
abstract: Pheophytin a was studied for its anti-inflammatory effects on macrophages. It was found to suppress key inflammatory mediators like nitric oxide and prostaglandin E2 by inhibiting specific signaling pathways.

title: Modulation of nitric oxide synthase activity in macrophages
authors: P. G. Jorens; K. E. Matthys; H. Bult
abstract: This review examines the induction and regulation of inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) in macrophages. It highlights how cytokines and other factors control NO release, a key molecule in host defense.

title: Anti-Inflammatory Cytokine Interleukin-4 Inhibits Inducible Nitric Oxide Synthase Gene Expression in the Mouse Macrophage Cell Line RAW264.7 through the Repression of Octamer-Dependent Transcription
authors: Miki Hiroi; Yoshiichi Sakaeda; Hana Yamaguchi; Yoshihiro Ohmori
id: Matched: 3.1. Inhibition of IFNγ- and/or LPS-Induced Nos2 mRNA Expression by IL
abstract: Interleukin-4's inhibition of inducible nitric oxide synthase gene expression in RAW264.7 cells was studied. IL-4 represses Oct-1-dependent transcription by competing for coactivators, thereby inhibiting iNOS.

abstract: This study investigated the effect of a mustard gas analog (CEES) on nitric oxide production in LPS-stimulated macrophages. CEES was found to inhibit nitric oxide synthesis by decreasing iNOS protein expression.

authors: Kyung-Ha Lee

abstract: The study investigated the internal ribosomal entry site (IRES) activity of nitric oxide synthase 2 (NOS2) mRNA. IRES-mediated translation of NOS2 mRNA is present in various cells and increases with LPS, partially maintaining nitrite production.

title: Hypoxia Aggravates Inhibition of Alveolar Epithelial Na-Transport by Lipopolysaccharide-Stimulation of Alveolar Macrophages
authors: Emel Baloglu; Kalpana Velineni; Ezgi Ermis-Kaya; Heimo Mairbäurl
abstract: Alveolar macrophages stimulated with LPS were studied for their effect on alveolar epithelial Na-transport, with and without hypoxia. LPS-stimulated macrophages impair Na-transport via NO-dependent mechanisms, and hypoxia exacerbates this inhibition.

title: Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Nitric Oxide, Prostaglandin E2, and Cytokine Production of Mouse and Human Macrophages Are Suppressed by Pheophytin-b
authors: Chun-Yu Lin; Wen-Hung Wang; Shin-Huei Chen; Yu-Wei Chang; Ling-Chien Hung; Chung-Yi Chen; Yen-Hsu Ch...
abstract: Pheophytin-b was studied for its anti-inflammatory effects on lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages. It suppressed nitric oxide, prostaglandin E2, and cytokine production by inhibiting STAT-1 and PI3K/Akt pathways.

title: Mannan-induced Nos2 in macrophages enhances IL-17–driven psoriatic arthritis by innate lymphocytes
authors: Jianghong Zhong; Tatjana Scholz; Anthony C. Y. Yau; Simon Guerard; Ulrike Hüffmeier; Harald Burkhard...
id: Matched: Deficiency of Nos2 alleviates MIP disease
abstract: Mannan stimulation of macrophages was studied for its role in psoriatic arthritis. Macrophage-derived nitric oxide enhances IL-17 release from innate lymphocytes, promoting the disease.

title: The inhibitory effect of quercitrin gallate on iNOS expression induced by lipopolysaccharide in Balb/c mice
authors: Hyun-Ye Jo; Youngsoo Kim; Sang-Yoon Nam; Beom Jun Lee; Yun-Bae Kim; Young Won Yun; Byeongwoo Ahn
abstract: Quercitrin gallate (QGR) was studied for its effect on nitric oxide (NO) and iNOS expression in LPS-stimulated mice. QGR significantly reduced LPS-induced NO production and iNOS expression, demonstrating anti-inflammatory potential.

title: Promoter of the mouse gene encoding calcium-independent nitric oxide synthase confers inducibility by interferon gamma and bacterial lipopolysaccharide
abstract: The promoter region of the mouse iNOS gene was cloned and analyzed for regulatory elements. This promoter confers inducibility by LPS and synergistic inducibility by IFN-gamma and LPS.

authors: Joshua T. Mattila; Anita C. Thomas

abstract: This paper examines the expression patterns of nitric oxide synthase (NOS) enzymes. It concludes that NOS isoforms may exhibit non-canonical expression, challenging established classifications.

title: Formulation of Gamma-Oryzanol Encapsulated Nanoparticles and Their Modulation Effects on Inducible Nitric Oxide Synthase and Nitric Oxide in LPS-Stimulated RAW 264.7 Macrophages
authors: Kornvipa Settakorn; Chuda Chittasupho; Weerasak Samee; Nut Koonrungsesomboon; Mingkwan Na Takuathung
abstract: Researchers developed gamma-oryzanol nanoparticles (ORZ-NPs) to improve stability and bioavailability. These nanoparticles effectively reduced nitric oxide synthase and nitric oxide production in stimulated macrophages. This suggests a targeted anti-inflammatory effect without impacting other key inflammatory cytokines.

abstract: Macrophages were precultured with low-dose LPS, then restimulated. This pretreatment selectively primes macrophages for differential responses to subsequent stimuli, rather than causing total refractoriness.

abstract: This study investigated how nitric oxide (NO) flux from inducible NO synthase (iNOS) affects proinflammatory macrophages. High NO flux, restricted to specific cells, limits hypoxic gradients and influences macrophage function, impacting tumor progression.
